plugins.name: topic-nudge
plugins.description: Shows a toast when a prompt starts a different topic than the earlier requests in the session, so you can /clear first

plugins.name: tokenscope-live
plugins.description: Live tokenscope pane: current intent, cost-weighted tokens, tests, edited files, alerts and recap for the session, fed by a local tokenscope live server

plugins.name: plugin-updates
plugins.description: Tells you when installed plugins or copied skills are behind upstream, without updating them

plugins.name: bedrock-meter
plugins.description: Token and USD meter for pay-per-token Amazon Bedrock sessions: a band above the prompt with cost, context, cache hit rate and today's total, priced at AWS's own Bedrock rates, plus a /bedrock-cost per-model pane.

plugins.name: evergreen-sessions
plugins.description: Pin important Claude Code sessions (/pin, /pins, /unpin): list them across every project with a resume command, and back up pinned transcripts so cleanupPeriodDays never deletes them

plugins.name: brewmod-plan-effort
plugins.description: While in plan mode, raises the main loop's request effort to a configurable level (default xhigh); never lowers it, subagents and the session effort setting untouched; /plan-effort

plugins.name: chrome-profile-names
plugins.description: Shows your Chrome profile names instead of 'Browser 1' and device IDs when Claude in Chrome lists or asks which connected browser to use; reads the local Chrome profile files only, marks browsers on other computers, no network or subprocess

plugins.name: checklist
plugins.description: A per-project checklist pane beside the chat that persists across sessions; /checklist adds, edits and marks items open, done or dropped, and Claude can read and update it through its own checklist tool; stored in the plugin store, no network or subprocess

plugins.name: loop-killer
plugins.description: Ends a stop-hook (e.g. /goal) re-prompt loop: after repeated re-prompt turns with no tool work, runs /goal clear and says so.

plugins.name: usage-hotkey
plugins.description: Screen-reader hotkey for Windows + NVDA: one key speaks context tokens, 5-hour and weekly usage with reset times, this conversation's share of each limit, and cost.

plugins.name: control-watch
plugins.description: A band above the prompt showing what Claude is controlling right now or in the last minute: your Chrome (Claude in Chrome), the built-in browser, desktop apps / your screen (computer use), Docker, simulators, terminals; a toast (and a macOS notification) when it takes over your real Chrome or a desktop app. Observe-only.

plugins.name: switchboard
plugins.description: A Board pane listing every local Claude Code session (Desktop Code tab and terminal) with its state: Needs You (permission prompt, question, API error) on top, then Working and Idle, with last-reply preview, branch/PR, context bar and background tasks; click to jump to the session (macOS; Desktop sessions on Windows). Observe-only; status reports are written under ~/.claude/switchboard/reports.

plugins.name: unattended
plugins.description: Stops a Claude Code session from asking you questions when nobody is at the keyboard: while on (/unattended, or launch with CLAUDE_UNATTENDED=1), AskUserQuestion and EnterPlanMode are denied with a note telling Claude to pick the most sensible option itself, say which and why, and carry on. Deny-only; no rewriting, no network.

plugins.name: worktrees
plugins.description: /worktrees docks a panel that lists every linked git worktree under your code folders (default ~/code) with a verdict (SAFE merged and clean, DIRTY, LOCAL ONLY, UNMERGED, LIVE session, MISSING), idle time, merge state against the target branches you pick (squash merges detected) and the Claude sessions that worked in it; tick the finished ones and delete them in one go. macOS only. Local git/find/stat/lsof scan; git fetch only when you press Fetch; delete asks first and only deletes merged branches. No network upload, no prompt or tool rewriting.

plugins.name: defer-tools
plugins.description: Moves six rarely used built-in tools (Workflow, ScheduleWakeup, ListAgents, CronCreate, CronDelete, CronList) behind ToolSearch by answering tool.describe with isDeferred: true, so their schemas only load into context the first time Claude calls them (author measured /context System tools 13.4k → 3.1k tokens). Tools stay usable; tools in permissions.deny stay removed. Only tool.describe; no network, no prompt or tool rewriting.

plugins.name: link-footer
plugins.description: Under each assistant reply in the terminal, lists every URL in it again as a one-row OSC 8 hyperlink with a short scheme-less label (middle of the path elided), so long URLs that wrap stay clickable and open the full address. Display only (ui.render AssistantMessage, calls next and appends rows); zero tokens, no network, the reply text Claude sees is unchanged.

plugins.name: ran-once
plugins.description: Guards against running a shell command twice by accident: once a bash/sh/zsh/shell code block from Claude's reply has run (its Run button in the Claude desktop app, or typed with ! at the prompt), that block is drawn dimmed and without its Run button; it stays selectable for copying. A later reply with the same command keeps its own Run button until that one runs. Reads only the session history, stores block keys in plugin state, no network, no model calls, no process, no prompt changes. Needs Claude Code 2.1.304+ for full effect.

plugins.name: code-tab-latex-fix
plugins.description: Makes LaTeX math in Claude's replies render in the Code tab of the Claude desktop app instead of showing as raw text: as the reply streams it adds the space the Code tab needs before inline \(...\), turns trivial formulas like \(n\) into plain text, and adjusts a few constructs the Code tab rejects. Only reply text is rewritten (before display and before it is saved to the transcript); inline code, fenced code blocks, thinking, tool calls and file writes are untouched. No network, no model calls, no process, no prompt changes.

plugins.name: dbview
plugins.description: Read-only PostgreSQL browser pane: /db opens a tree of your saved connections and local Docker Postgres containers, drilling down from databases and schemas to tables, showing columns, constraints, indexes, sample rows and DDL. Every query runs through local psql with default_transaction_read_only=on and a statement timeout; Docker containers are reached with docker exec. URLs saved with /db connect (including any password) are kept in plugin storage; the password is passed via PGPASSWORD, never on the command line. No network beyond the database connection itself, no model calls, no prompt changes.

plugins.name: callout-colors
plugins.description: Makes the parts of long replies you must not miss stand out: sections headed 'Decision for you', 'Needs your input', 'Your call' are drawn in a bordered box in the theme's warning color, 'Summary', 'TL;DR' and 'Recap' sections (and the engine's between-tool-call summaries) in the suggestion color. Subagent (Agent/Task) calls and results get an indented left rail in a per-agent color so each call pairs with its result and parallel agents stay apart, with a compact one-line identity and outcome (tools, tokens, time, report first line); ctrl+o keeps the engine's expanded view. Display only (ui.render): the stored conversation and what Claude sees are unchanged. No commands, no network, no model calls, no processes.

plugins.name: adhd-reader-zh
plugins.description: Chinese-capable edition of ADHD Reader: bolds the start of each word in Claude's replies so long answers are easier to scan, splitting Simplified and Traditional Chinese into words first with the built-in Intl.Segmenter (unknown words are read two characters at a time); on/off button and 5 strength levels above the prompt, /adhd to toggle. Display only: rewrites how replies are rendered, not the conversation; no external programs, no network. Based on UBRN/adhd-reader (MIT).

plugins.name: keep-awake-linux
plugins.description: Prevents Linux system idle/sleep while Claude Code is actively working: each turn start, tool call and turn end renews a systemd-inhibit lock, released after a configurable idle time (default 30 minutes) or on session exit; /keep-awake-info shows in a live pane which Claude sessions block sleep. Linux with systemd only; runs systemd-inhibit and ps locally, no network.

plugins.name: cargo-progress
plugins.description: Shows cargo's progress bar under a running cargo command instead of a line per crate, and leaves a short result note when it finishes (build errors/lint errors/warnings and time, or tests passed/failed/ignored with failing names). Transparently wraps Bash commands that call cargo in a shell function that runs the mod's bundled perl script (bin/cargo-progress.pl); Claude still gets cargo's normal output and exit code. Permission denies for the original command still apply; never allows a call itself. Needs perl (falls back to plain cargo without it); no network.

plugins.name: smart-rtl
plugins.description: Right-to-left (Hebrew, Arabic, Persian) layout for Claude Code in the Claude desktop app and other non-terminal surfaces: per paragraph/list/table direction detection, expressed with Unicode bidi controls in the rendered text; inline code, math and LaTeX stay left-to-right, code blocks are untouched, and your own RTL prompts are right-aligned. /rtl toggles it (remembered in $.store). Display only (ui.render on AssistantMessage/UserMessage); the terminal is left alone (complements the terminal rtl mod). /ltr (Windows only) runs the bundled windows/claude-ltr.ps1, which closes Claude Desktop and restarts it with --force-ui-direction=ltr. No network, no model calls.

plugins.name: aws-guard
plugins.description: Denies AWS CLI calls that delete IAM roles or policies (iam delete-role*/delete-policy*), change AWS Organizations (any organizations operation other than describe-*/list-*), or destroy KMS keys (schedule-key-deletion, delete-imported-key-material), and tells Claude to hand you the exact command to run yourself with the ! prefix. Finds the aws call through bash -c, env, xargs, sudo, subshells, command substitutions and PowerShell wrappers; help and --generate-cli-skeleton pass. Deny only, never rewrites or allows a command. Reads the command line as written (no variable/alias expansion; AWS Tools for PowerShell cmdlets and SDK scripts are not checked), so it is a guardrail, not a security boundary. No network.

plugins.name: tf-plan-summary
plugins.description: Gives Claude a plan_summary tool for a saved Terraform plan (terraform plan -out=FILE): it runs terraform show -json locally and returns only a few lines - counts to add/change/replace/destroy/import/forget, drift, every destroy and replace (with the attributes forcing a replace), IAM/KMS/security group/S3 policy and other security-sensitive changes listed by attribute name only (never values), and changing outputs - so the model does not read the raw plan. Needs terraform on PATH; runs it via $.process.spawn without a shell; on failure returns only terraform's first Error line. No network, no model calls.

plugins.name: output-trimmer
plugins.description: Keeps long output of noisy commands out of the model's context: for terraform/tofu init/plan/apply/destroy/import/refresh, checkov/trivy/tfsec/prowler, npm/pnpm/yarn/bun/pip/uv/poetry installs and docker build/pull/compose, output over 120 lines is cut in the result Claude sees to the first 15 lines, up to 30 error/warning lines from the middle, and the last 40 lines, with a note giving the path of the full output. Rewrites only those tool results (never the command); the full stdout/stderr is written first to claude-output/ under $TEMP/$TMPDIR (or /tmp), and if that write fails the result is returned untouched; files are left to OS temp cleanup. No network.

plugins.name: litellm-key
plugins.description: For people who reach Claude through a LiteLLM proxy: a status line and /litellm pane with the virtual key's budget, spend, rate limits, expiry, models and 30 days of usage, a band above the prompt while a budget is used up, and warning toasts. Admins can create/edit/block keys, grant budget and read router fallbacks, each change confirmed in a dialog first. Talks only to the proxy Claude Code already uses (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL or litellm_url); /litellm share hands a report to Claude only when you run it.

plugins.name: clipring
plugins.description: A kill ring for the prompt box: alt+backspace cuts the selection or the cursor's line (consecutive cuts merge, Emacs-style), ctrl+alt+backspace cuts the whole draft, and text killed with ctrl+u / ctrl+k is captured too; up to 50 clips persist across sessions in the plugin store and the latest cut also goes to the system clipboard. A band above the prompt shows the selected clip (alt+up/down to pick, alt+v to paste at the cursor, alt+d to delete); /clips or alt+c opens a pane listing every clip (enter pastes), alt+h shows help. All chords are configurable via plugin options. Only edits the draft in the prompt box when you press its keys (prompt.edit / prompt.fill insert, never submits); no network, no model calls, no child processes.

plugins.name: query-guard
plugins.description: Holds risky database commands that Claude runs through Bash (sqlite3, psql, mysql, snowsql, databricks CLI, dbt) until you choose: DROP TABLE/DATABASE/SCHEMA, TRUNCATE, DELETE or UPDATE without WHERE, ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN, dbt --full-refresh, and any command whose host, URL, connection, profile or dbt target names prod/production. A pane (or a band above the prompt on narrow terminals) shows the command, why it was held, the targets and, for local SQLite files, the current row count; Proceed (1) runs the command unchanged, Cancel (2) or closing the pane denies it. A status line counts held commands. Only waits/denies, never rewrites the command; runs only `sqlite3 -readonly ... SELECT COUNT(*)` on local SQLite files and `sleep` while waiting; no network, no model calls.

plugins.name: agent-trace
plugins.description: Adds a trace pane (/agent-trace, titled 轨迹) showing what the agent did this session as a Langfuse-style tree: turns → model steps → the tool calls each step asked for → subagent runs nested under the Agent call that spawned them. Each model step shows the messages it added since the previous request, tokens, cache hit (yellow under 50%, ⚠ when uncached input jumps 3×), time to first token, tok/s, thinking and reply preview; per-tool stats (count/total/average/failures), a clickable 3-lane timeline, and search. Observe-only: turn.step passes every stream chunk through unchanged, tool.call records and returns the result unchanged; optional captureSystemPrompt (off by default) only reads the prompt.compose result and returns it unchanged. Records live in session state (max 2000 rows, full payloads of the latest 150, each block clipped); no network, no child processes, no model calls.

plugins.name: session-load
plugins.description: A band above the prompt for people running many Claude Code sessions on a Mac: CPU and memory column charts grouped by Claude Code session (each session plus everything it started: shells, test runs, dev servers, subagent tools), with a 90-second trend; processes still running after their session ended (grouped by worktree, yellow); Claude's own helpers in grey; and work in progress — test/lint/build/deploy commands running on the machine, in-progress GitHub Actions runs for the session's repo, and running subagents — with percent done and time left estimated from previous run durations. macOS only. Polls fixed read-only commands (ps, memory_pressure, sysctl every 3 s; ~/.claude/sessions/*.json every 15 s; `gh run list` in the session cwd every 30 s, using your local gh login, only to read Actions status). Hooks pass through unchanged (session.start calls next first; ui.render keeps next(e) below the band). Duration history in the plugin store; no model calls, no session content sent anywhere.

plugins.name: brainless-claude-progress
plugins.description: A progress pane (/progress) and a one-line status-line summary for the current ticket: steps Write → Review → Verify → CI → Merge, CI status with time estimates learned from past runs (medians), running background agents and bash tasks, and a 'Your turn' marker when Claude is waiting on you. Reads PR/CI state with fixed read-only gh commands (gh pr view, gh pr list --state merged, gh repo view) using your local gh login. Hooks only observe: tool.call calls next first; prompt.submit only detects the UI language and passes the prompt through unchanged. Animated spark can be turned off with /progress still. UI in English, 繁體中文, 简体中文, 日本語. No model calls, no network besides gh, no session content sent anywhere.

plugins.name: errfold
plugins.description: Folds failed tool calls to a single red line in the transcript (✗ tool, short input, first error line; ctrl+o expands the full output) and keeps a session log of tool errors: /errors toggles a pane listing them newest first (lines per error configurable, c clears), and the status line shows '✗ n tool errors'. Display-only: tool.call passes every call through unchanged and only records failures; the log lives in memory only; no network, no model calls, no child processes.

plugins.name: context-canary
plugins.description: Makes instruction drift visible in long sessions: /canary setup (after asking for consent) adds a rule to CLAUDE.md that every final answer must start with a sentinel (default 🐤), optionally with 1–5 checkpoint words spread through the file. When an answer misses it, a small canary above the prompt dies, a notice names the missing part, and by default the built-in session compaction runs with instructions to keep your rules; a second miss within 30 minutes locks automatic compaction. /canary log lists the last 30 misses. Reads answer text on turn.complete and only appends a one-line note; writes only CLAUDE.md (with consent) and its own store; no network, no model calls, no child processes, no prompt rewriting.

plugins.name: lean-comments
plugins.description: Checks every Edit and Write Claude makes and refuses changes that add banner/divider comments, multi-line comments (including multi-line /** */ doc blocks unless allowDocComments is on), comments over 120 characters, narrating or labelling comments ("Step 1: …", "# Helpers"), or more than 3 new comments in one change, so Claude rewrites it with only short why-comments. Only comments the change adds are checked; tool directives (eslint-disable, @ts-expect-error, noqa, license headers, …) are never flagged; Markdown/prose files are skipped. Settings: mode block (default) / warn / off, maxLength, maxNewComments, allowDocComments. Deny-only by default (warn mode lets the edit through and appends a note to the tool result); no network, no model calls, no child processes, no prompt rewriting.

plugins.name: extended-polls
plugins.description: Gives Claude a poll tool (mcp__extended-polls__ask) for up to 30 multiple-choice questions on one screen (configurable 1-100; 2-10 options each, single or multi-select, optional recommended option and a free-text Other field), answered in a keyboard-first pane beside the conversation, so a batch of planning decisions can be settled at once instead of AskUserQuestion's 4 questions x 4 options. The call waits until you press Submit or Cancel (closing the pane only hides it; a band above the prompt or /poll brings it back), then Claude gets every answer, unanswered ones as skipped. 22 interface languages. Runs a small local /bin/sh waiter in a temp dir to hold the call open; no network, no model calls, no prompt rewriting, does not touch other tools.

plugins.name: leaks
plugins.description: Finds where your Claude Code week went: /leaks opens a pane that replays the last 7 days of local transcripts (~/.claude/projects, /leaks --days 30 for more) and ranks the avoidable spend at API prices — sessions running past the compact point, cache rebuilt after a break, read-only subagents on a big model, subagent caches expiring between steps, huge tool outputs re-read every turn — each with the fix; a setting (e.g. autoCompactWindow) or a CLAUDE.md line applies with one press (a), writing ~/.claude/settings.json or ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md only when you press it. A strip above the prompt flags a leak as it happens (context past warn_at, default 400k, or a 1h cache about to expire / expired on a big conversation, with the re-write cost) with compact now / hide buttons. Runs the bundled leaks.mjs with local node (Node 22+); no network, no model calls, no prompt rewriting.

plugins.name: view-memory
plugins.description: /view-memory opens a Memory pane over every project's Claude Code auto-memory folder (~/.claude/projects/*/memory), not only the current one: search across all memory files, an Overdue list of lines whose `due YYYY-MM-DD` has passed, per-folder health (files MEMORY.md doesn't link, dead links, missing files in symlinked folders), and what each session here loads (CLAUDE.md files and MEMORY.md with token sizes). Once a reply re-reads more than 150k tokens it shows a one-time toast suggesting saving memory and /clear. Read-only: only reads local files and runs `git rev-parse` to find the repo root; prompt.context is observed only (result returned unchanged); no network, no model calls, no prompt rewriting.

plugins.name: agent-atc
plugins.description: Air-traffic control for subagents: /atc opens a pane listing every subagent as a tree (status, elapsed time, current tool call; 'quiet' when a running agent has made no tool call for 90s), pick one with 1-9 to see its model, call count, tokens, recent tool trail and final answer, then type a message to it (or a follow-up to a finished agent) or press Stop. Status line shows the running count; optionally auto-opens on the first subagent on wide terminals. Messages go only to the picked agent via $.session.send when you press Send; Stop calls the built-in TaskStop only when you press it; tool.call/agent.spawn/turn.complete are observed and passed through unchanged; no network, no model calls, no external programs, no prompt rewriting.

plugins.name: context-rings
plugins.description: A row of rings above the prompt, one per recent Claude Code session on this machine, filled by how much of its context window is used (yellow/red at 50%/80% by default, against a configurable 100K-1M window); newest activity first, up to ten plus a +N, hover for name, folder, tokens and working/idle/closed; an All/this-folder chip filters. Subagents show as small dots once they pass 75% of a 500K limit, with one toast at 90%. A ring flashes shortly before its session's 1-hour or 5-minute prompt cache expires, so you can reply or /compact first. Reads ~/.claude/sessions/*.json and the tail of recently changed transcripts every 5 s via fixed read-only ps/find/stat/tail (BSD stat -f, so effectively macOS only); stores only session names and toasted subagents; every hook passes events through unchanged; no network, no model calls, no prompt rewriting.

plugins.name: sf-headless-band
plugins.description: Shows your Salesforce CLI default org above the prompt with its type pill (scratch, developer edition, sandbox, production in red) and a scratch org's days to expiry, plus every Salesforce DX / Hosted MCP server added to Claude Code and the orgs each can reach, with a connected check mark. Hidden until you run /sf-headless-band (on|off|toggle). Read-only: reads the sf CLI config, aliases and org auth files under ~/.sf and ~/.sfdx (only org type, instance URL and expiry are used), sfdx-project.json and Claude Code's MCP config (~/.claude.json, .mcp.json); refreshes every 15 s and when those files change; tool.call only watches mcp__ calls for the My Domain they carry and returns results unchanged; no processes, no network, no model calls, no prompt rewriting.

plugins.name: usage-meter
plugins.description: Status line with this session's spend, its $/hour over the last hour, and every open session's $/hour combined. Toasts when all sessions together pass a $/hour budget (default $40/h, at most every 30 min), at three compactions within 30 minutes (context refilling fast), and when Haiku runs past 100K context; /spend ranks open sessions by $/hour with total spend, context size and model. Spend is Claude Code's own session cost figure at API prices (read it as relative usage on a subscription). Sessions share readings through the mod's own $.store; thresholds are constants at the top of hooks/register.ts. Hooks turn.complete, session.compact and its own /spend command only; writes no files, no processes, no network, no model calls, no prompt rewriting.

plugins.name: gh-refs
plugins.description: When a Claude reply mentions GitHub issues or PRs (full URLs, owner/repo#N, or a bare #N resolved to the reply's last named repo, the Default repository setting, or the session folder's GitHub repo), shows a row of chips under the reply colored by state; hovering a chip shows title, issue/PR, state (open/closed/merged/draft/not planned), milestone, labels, parent theme and a one- or two-line body summary. Fetches with your local gh CLI (one gh api graphql call per batch, cached 5 minutes in the mod's $.state); only the issue/PR references are sent to GitHub, never conversation text. Render-only (ui.render AssistantMessage) plus session.start; no prompt rewriting, no model calls, no file writes. Requires gh signed in.

plugins.name: meter
plugins.description: A side pane (/meter) with context fill and compaction point, cache hit rate, 5-hour and weekly rate-limit use with burn pace (percent used vs share of the window elapsed, colored green/yellow/red, with a projected time of hitting 100% when pace is above 1), session cost, and the largest context categories (messages, MCP tools, agents, skills, memory files, per MCP server). Drawn outside the model's context, so it adds no tokens. /meter refresh takes a full count; optional meterAutoOpen opens it at session start on wide terminals. Needs Claude Code 2.1.302+. Uses only $.session.usage, session.measure, $.ui panes, $.clock and its own /meter command; writes no files, no processes, no network, no model calls, no prompt rewriting.

plugins.name: codex-monitor
plugins.description: A pane (/codex-monitor) that shows, live, the Codex work this Claude session sent out: jobs from the openai codex-plugin-cc (/codex:rescue etc., matched by the plugin's state.json sessionId), codex exec runs from Bash/PowerShell (registered when the command is sent and matched to the rollout by its first prompt), and claude-codex-bridge codex_message_send threads. Splits up to 4 running jobs, shows each turn's commands with exit codes and Codex's replies, a job list you can click to pin, paging buttons, a status-line count and a toast when each Codex turn finishes. Read-only: polls ~/.codex/sessions rollout files every 3 s with $.fs.read (large files via local tail/head/base64 on macOS/Linux or pwsh on Windows); tool.call is only observed and passed through unchanged. No network, no model calls, no prompt rewriting, no file writes.

plugins.name: repo-spend
plugins.description: A band above the prompt showing what your Claude Code sessions have cost in the current repo (main checkout and its worktrees; each session's spend is attributed to the repo where the work happened), today and over the last 7 days, plus this session's live cost, burn rate over the last 30 minutes and a sparkline. On Pro/Max it shows API-price equivalents. A weekly archive keeps totals after Claude Code deletes old logs. /repo-spend hides or shows the band. Local only: runs local git rev-parse and the bundled python3 scan.py over ~/.claude/projects logs (cache in ~/.cache/claude-repo-spend, archive in ~/.local/share/claude-repo-spend). No network, no model calls, no prompt or tool rewriting. Needs python3.

plugins.name: blast-radius-win
plugins.description: Windows/PowerShell-ready fork of the official Blast Radius mod: holds risky Bash, PowerShell and Monitor commands (rm -rf, Remove-Item -Recurse, git reset --hard, git clean, force push, migrations), measures what they would delete or change, and waits for Proceed or Cancel in a pane (Cancel pre-selected; falls back to a band above the prompt). Fails closed: if the mod errors, the command is refused. tool.call only denies or passes the call through unchanged, never rewrites it. Measuring is read-only: local git (fsmonitor off), Git's bash find/du, or powershell.exe with paths passed as JSON on stdin; never runs project tools. No network, no model calls.

plugins.name: agy-lead
plugins.description: /agy 面板实时显示 Antigravity CLI（agy）的执行步骤、被拒命令和回复；配套 skill 让 Claude 规划、写 brief，并在 git worktree 里审查 agy 的改动。

plugins.name: ask-preview-text
plugins.description: 让 AskUserQuestion 的选项预览能被读屏软件读：把预览从对话框里拿掉（对话框变成普通竖排选项列表），在对话记录里该问题下方一次性以纯文本列出所有预览（编号与选项对应）。只改显示，不改答案；mod 出错时原样交回自带对话框。

plugins.name: commit-gate
plugins.description: 拦下 git commit，直到你批准：你最近一条提示里说了 go / commit it，或对 Claude 的提交提问回答了 yes；否则弹出对话框（默认选 Not yet）。提交后若又编辑了文件，需要重新批准。只 deny/询问，不改写命令；prompt.submit 只记录批准状态，不改写提示、不注入上下文；不联网、不调模型。

plugins.name: uptick
plugins.description: /uptick pane listing updates for Claude Code, plugins, skills-CLI skills and Homebrew; runs an update only after you confirm the exact command

plugins.name: read-budget
plugins.description: Refuses the third full Read of the same large, unchanged file in a session and points Claude to Grep or a ranged Read

plugins.name: nvim-inline-review
plugins.description: Snapshots each file before Claude's first Edit/Write/NotebookEdit so the claude-inline-review.nvim Neovim plugin can review Claude's changes hunk by hunk in your real buffers
